scenes.headline: How a 40-step image model learns to finish in 6
scenes.sub: Two distilled adapters, and a speedup that is steps alone.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fennel! Qwen Image two point one paints in forty steps. Two teams taught it to finish in six.

scenes.text: Train a small adapter so the model takes a few big steps along its own curved path, not forty small ones.
scenes.say: The idea: a small adapter lets the model take a few big steps instead of forty small ones.

scenes.title: One Euler step
scenes.say: Sampling walks from noise to an image in straight steps.

parts.note: the denoiser's predicted velocity: one forward pass
parts.say: v is the denoiser's velocity. Each step is one forward pass.

parts.note: the step size; the direction is held fixed across it
parts.say: Each step holds that direction fixed. The path bends, so big steps overshoot.

left.title: The 40-step base
items: Classifier-free guidance already off by default
left.say: The base takes forty steps, one pass each. Guidance is already off.

right.title: A distilled student
right.say: The student takes six, so at best it is six point six seven times faster.

items.text: The student draws in few steps
items.say: The student draws an image in a few steps.
Noise it again. The teacher and a critic each say where it should go.
Push the student along the difference.
Then check that seeds still differ. Early students lost a quarter of their diversity.

steps.say: Inside the denoiser: a timestep embedder, a shared modulation, and thirty-two blocks.
Both students add a low-rank side branch to attention and feed-forward.

steps.note: only the rank-256 adapter reaches here
steps.say: The larger one also reaches the timestep path.

steps.note: unmerged: exact, but each step costs more
steps.say: Both run unmerged. Exact, but every step costs a little more.

scenes.title: Measured speedup, end to end
scenes.note: Publishers' own timings, on different GPUs
scenes.say: Six steps measured five point oh two times faster. The six point three headline is the weaker adapter, at an untrained size.

steps.say: The cost shows in small text. Here is the base, at forty steps.
At six steps, letters print twice.
Eight steps helps. The base still reads best.

scenes.text: With guidance already off, a few-step student's speedup is the step ratio, minus fixed costs and adapter overhead.
scenes.say: With guidance already off, the speedup is the step ratio, minus fixed costs.

recap: Curved paths need small Euler steps
scenes.say: To recap: curved paths need small steps, both students are distilled adapters, and the speedup is steps alone.
